subject: Discovery recap + procurement framing — Omega Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rojas <elena@omega-corp.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 20:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + procurement framing — Omega Corp

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Great to meet you and hear more about the generative features your team is planning for the customer portal. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned going into the technical deep-dive: 

Pain points you shared
- Highly variable inference latency for customer-facing prompts (spikes during peak traffic).
- Current per-token cost from self-hosted endpoints is driving CPU/GPU budget overruns.
- Lack of clear rollout process for models across environments (staging -> prod) and no consistent observability across routes.

Current stack
- In-house Triton-based endpoints deployed on EKS for low-latency routes.
- OpenAI for burst/exploratory usage.
- Postgres + Redis for session and KV storage.

Success criteria you listed
- 95th percentile latency < 200ms for interactive prompts under target load.
- Predictable unit cost (goal: reduce per-token inference spend by ~30% vs current ops).
- Auditability: audit logs, model version pinning, and SOC2-level controls for PII paths.

Procurement / decision process (what we heard)
- Primary decision maker: Elena Rojas (Product) — product/engineering will validate performance.
- Procurement / legal owner: Michael Chen (Procurement) — will handle contract and security checklist.
- Timeline: target commercial decision & pilot kickoff by end of Q2 (June).

Initial commercial guardrails we suggest to keep conversations efficient
- Pilot: 3 months with defined SLOs and usage cap (we typically recommend a 100k token/day baseline for performance validation).
- Pricing: we’ll propose a pilot pricing range and an optional committed-rate discount if you commit to a monthly usage tier (we’ll share a preliminary guardrail range in the SE follow-up).
- Security: SOC2 + customer-managed keys (optional) for production; we’ll flag any additional controls your security team requests.

Next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Ethan (SE) — propose Tue 2026-04-06 or Wed 2026-04-07, 60–90m. He can bring latency profiling and a plan for a short benchmarking test.
2) I’ll attach a one-page recap + initial commercial guardrail ranges and our standard pilot SOW outline (attached).
3) Michael — if you can share a procurement timeline and any mandatory contract terms (e.g., PO vs SOW, required indemnities), we’ll surface those in the next doc/quote.

Attachments: Redwood-Discovery-Recap-Omega-20260401.pdf (summary + guardrails), Omega-Procurement-Questionnaire.xlsx (for procurement).

If this looks correct I’ll lock in the SE call and have Ethan follow up with a proposed agenda for the deep-dive.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform for production LLMs

- Stakeholders: correct on the list — I’m the product lead, engineering (Victor Lee) will validate the performance work, and Michael will own procurement/legal. I added Michael on the cc.
- Timeline: end of Q2 is correct; we’re hoping to start a limited pilot by July.
- Pilot sizing: 100k tokens/day sounds reasonable for benchmarking.

Can we do the SE deep-dive on Tue 2026-04-06 at 2pm PT? That works for our engineering lead as well. Please send calendar invite and an agenda.

Michael — I’ve attached our procurement questionnaire (filled with the basics) — you may want to add anything else separately.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa/Elena — looping in a couple quick procurement items so we can keep the timeline tight: 

1) Can Redwood provide a high-level pricing range for the pilot (ballpark monthly cost for 100k tokens/day) and any options for committed discounts? We understand this will be a rough estimate; a range is fine.
2) SOC2 report and any whitepapers on data handling — required for our security intake.
3) Contract vehicle: we prefer an SOW with a PO; please flag any redline items we should expect.

If you can share the ballpark pricing and SOC2 evidence this week it will help us get internal signoff to kick off the pilot planning.
